headline: On a real 400-tile page `@yak/solid` folds all but the rating bar, and the one dynamic value left is enough to put it behind hand-written Solid by a factor of five.

microbench.why: `vanilla-solid` leads at 599,000 renders/s, more than twice `vanilla`'s 228,000, because eleven elements per tile is where Solid's template cloning beats React's element creation. `next-yak-css` at 230,000 and `stylex-layers` at 206,000 head the React field. `yak-solid` at 105,000 folds every static primitive — its lib self-time is 0.531 ms of a 5.35 ms render — but `RatingFill` carries a dynamic width, so one element per tile takes the reactive path and costs more than the other ten together. `emotion` at 30,400 and `styled-components` at 52,400 serialize eleven rule sets per tile.

autocannon.why: `vanilla-solid` at 432 req/s leads, `vanilla` at 255 and `next-yak-css` at 247 follow. `panda-props` at 52 req/s resolves eleven style objects per tile inside each request.

attribution.why: `vanilla-solid` renders in 1.09 ms against 2.14 ms for `vanilla` — half of that gap is framework, 0.613 ms versus 1.88 ms. `next-yak-css` at 2.19 ms and `next-yak` at 2.52 ms follow, the latter booking 0.681 ms of lib for its unfolded primitives. `cn` at 2.82 ms edges `cnfast` at 3.23 ms, both resolving eleven cached class lists per tile against `tailwind-merge`'s 4.97 ms with 1.91 ms of its own runtime. `emotion` books 8.62 ms of lib, and `panda-props` 10.9 ms of component self-time.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` at 55.2 ms, `vanilla` at 57.3 ms and `panda` at 57.3 ms finish within noise of each other. `styled-components` at 244 ms and `goober` at 258 ms attach a large sheet as they hydrate.

inp.why: Ten lanes answer between 8.3 ms and 10.7 ms, flat given the spread. `emotion` at 52.4 ms and `panda-props` at 41.2 ms re-resolve every tile's styles on the update.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 43.5 ms and `yak-solid` in 75.9 ms, against 129 ms for `vanilla` and 241 ms for `emotion`. Building 4,400 elements is where template cloning pays off most, and the 32 ms between the two Solid lanes is the rating bar's reactive wrapper.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane near 0.68 ms. Container queries and hover guards make the match more expensive than a button, and every lane pays the same.

payload.why: The next-yak css-prop lanes lead at 7,475 gz B with `vanilla` at 7,790 B. `yak-solid` reaches 15,326 B, with 10,684 B of HTML: eleven elements per tile, each carrying a hydration key, is the shape where Solid's markup cost compounds fastest. `cn` at 29,178 B is the heaviest lane in the suite, its class lists landing in both the markup and a 13 kB merge runtime.

nsweep.why: `vanilla-solid` holds 6.28 ms at the largest size against 17.8 ms for `vanilla` and 22.2 ms for `next-yak`. `emotion` at 133 ms and `panda-props` at 145 ms bend hardest.

crossCase: Paired with the Example `multifile-shop`, which is this page with the primitives split across modules. `yak-solid` moves 105,000 to 11,500 renders/s — a factor of nine, the largest module-boundary penalty any lane shows, because every primitive that crosses the boundary loses its fold and becomes a Solid component per element. `next-yak` moves 195,000 to 101,000 for the same reason, and `vanilla-solid` moves 599,000 to 500,000, which is what the split costs when no compiler is involved.
